commits.author: Gonçalo Simões Pereira
commits.message:
test: run every level of the error and union based sql injection against the seed data (#815)

The existing tests mock JdbcTemplate, so the query of a level and the code
that reads its result never run. Run each level against the real schema
and seed data instead, the same way AuthSeedDataRegressionTest does.

- levels meant to be injectable are proven to be: another row, another
  table through union and, for the error based ones, the data of the
  database inside the error that is returned
- levels that are not injectable are proven not to leak, without fixing
  how they answer an unknown id

commits.author: Gonçalo Simões Pereira
commits.message:
fix: reject path traversal in PreflightController before reading the file (#818)

* fix: reject a path traversal filename in PreflightController before reading it

PreflightController serves back a file previously stored under
UnrestrictedFileUpload's content disposition root, resolving the path
variable directly with Path#resolve and no check that the result still
falls under that root.

Tested against a running instance: Tomcat/Spring already reject a plain
"..", url-encoded, double-encoded, backslash, encoded-slash, null-byte and
overlong-UTF-8 traversal in this path variable (400/404), so the read side
was not reproducible as filed in #344. The write side is a separate,
intended vulnerability (LEVEL_8/9 of UnrestrictedFileUpload write the
upload wherever an unvalidated filename says to, by design).

Relying only on the container for this is fragile: a different Tomcat
version, a reverse proxy, or a loosened URL-decoding setting could let a
traversal filename through. Normalize the resolved path and reject it with
404 if it is not under the content disposition root, the same outcome a
missing file already produces, before ever opening a FileInputStream.

* test: fix flaky outside-root file and an overclaiming test in PreflightControllerTest

- use Files.createTempFile for the outside-root file instead of a fixed
  name, a leftover file from an earlier run could otherwise get truncated
  and then deleted by this test
- the MockMvc test for a literal ".." claimed to prove the new containment
  check runs, but verified empirically (by removing the check) that
  Spring's own routing normalizes a raw ".." segment away before the
  request ever reaches the controller, so it was proving routing
  behaviour, not the check. Renamed it to say that and point at the direct
  fetchFile(..) calls above, which do exercise the check (confirmed the
  same way, they fail without it)

commits.author: Gonçalo Simões Pereira
commits.message:
fix: strip translator instruction from HEADER_INJECTION_VULNERABILITY (#817)

messages_bn_IN.properties and messages_mr_IN.properties carried a second
sentence after the translated description, written for the translator
("all keys such as INVALID_END_POINT, XSS_VULNERABILITY etc. must remain
unchanged") rather than for the reader. The key is the description of an
@AttackVector in JWTVulnerability, so it is served to users browsing the
JWT module in either language. Removed the sentence, kept the translation.
